chapter: Lover Man and the postwar years
title: Milt Gabler, Eddie Heywood and Billie Holiday refusing the second song
summary: Gabler took Ramirez's arrangements unpaid; Heywood made the first instrumental "Lover Man"; Billie balked at doing both numbers.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: So... They didn't pay me for the arrangements for Larry Adler's "Begin The Beguine" -- Milt Gabler took both. Now, he recorded Eddie Heywood... You know, at that time Eddie Heywood was very hot with "Begin The Beguine." He had recorded Eddie Heywood on a 12-incher, and Eddie was the first one to record, to make a commercial record of "Lover Man." Actually, also Billie Holiday, because when he made the 10-incher (in those days, the 10-inch records were out), "Lover Man" was on the other side. Well, he inveigled Billie Holiday to do this number, because this... Willie Dukes sang like her, only stronger than her. Imitation is a strong flattery, isn't it...
So anyway, she came up and she was to do the two numbers. But she says, "No, I don't want to do the two numbers; Ram will make too much money."
Well, I mean, she was a child at heart. But I have a witness to that. Walter saw (?). He just couldn't get over that.
